partners.mechanism_chain: GATAD2B (HGNC:21903) —DISRUPTS→ Transcriptional Regulation (GO:0006355); Transcriptional Regulation (GO:0006355) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual Disability (HP:0001249); PPARG (HGNC:9217) —DISRUPTS→ Lipid Metabolism and Adipogenesis (GO:0006629); Lipid Metabolism and Adipogenesis (GO:0006629) —LEADS_TO→ Partial Lipodystrophy (HP:0001026); Lipid Metabolism and Adipogenesis (GO:0006629) —LEADS_TO→ Metabolic Dysregulation (HP:0012757). While GATAD2B (causative for MONDO:0014034) and PPARG (causative for MONDO:0011448) are distinct genes, their downstream effects converge on broader biological processes. GATAD2B's role in transcriptional regulation impacts neuronal development, leading to intellectual disability. PPARG's critical role in lipid metabolism and adipogenesis, when disrupted, causes partial lipodystrophy and metabolic dysregulation. The overlap lies in the disruption of complex cellular processes, where the disruption of transcriptional regulation (GATAD2B) can indirectly affect metabolic pathways, and the disruption of lipid metabolism (PPARG) can lead to systemic metabolic consequences that may manifest with some overlapping features or secondary effects on overall cellular health, though not a direct molecular convergence.
